### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**13** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **1** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 30a8047bad6e264762dd41ded7f1290c1224afc6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2532b7dcd19ca004dc22b284fb0ae4091b24e3bc` — the merge of head `c6ffc0b81395dfa7008fcf2de3c1c042498c7888` into base `30a8047bad6e264762dd41ded7f1290c1224afc6`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2532b7dcd19ca004dc22b284fb0ae4091b24e3bc && git checkout 2532b7dcd19ca004dc22b284fb0ae4091b24e3bc
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 30a8047bad6e264762dd41ded7f1290c1224afc6 c6ffc0b81395dfa7008fcf2de3c1c042498c7888 && git checkout -B drift-repro 30a8047bad6e264762dd41ded7f1290c1224afc6 && git merge --no-ff c6ffc0b81395dfa7008fcf2de3c1c042498c7888

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 30a8047bad6e264762dd41ded7f1290c1224afc6
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

**L1 verdict (L1-a): ACCEPT** at head `c6ffc0b81395dfa7008fcf2de3c1c042498c7888` (Fixes #37980). Full read · 2026-11-27T15:49Z

## 席位核对

**Shape and gates.** 6 files, +197/-19. Check-runs at c6ffc0b8: 33 success, 16 expected skip, 0 failed. Mergeable state is clean. Not governed. `Clause-②: no` · `Metadata-protocol: none`. `l1-face` is CLEAN on 13 items. No contract review is owed, since this is not a narrowing and no governed path is touched.

**What I read myself.**
- **Key spelling.** The PR takes `BUNDLE/FILE_STEM#ID` instead of the card's example `BUNDLE:ID`, and the card left the spelling to the author. The reason given holds: I counted ids repeating across eval files in 10 of the 14 bundles on this head. The key is `caseKey` from `cases.ts:88`, the same string the summary and records print, so a key copied from a summary works. The README example `objectstack-ai/skills-tools-knowledge#6` names a real case.
- **`selectCases`.** It narrows `selectBundles`' answer, which holds every case of the selected bundles, so a key fails the selection only for a reason the refusal chain names. The checks run in order: bundle, then `--skills` membership, then eval file, then id. Each refusal lists what exists. The plan keeps catalog order, and duplicates are folded in the parser. `planRound` is unchanged, so a behaviour case runs both arms and a trigger case runs the with-skill arm.
- **Flags.** Refused beside `--regrade`, `--self-test` and `--triggers-only`, the same way `--triggers-only` is refused. An empty or misshaped value is refused by `CASE_KEY_SHAPE`. Accepted beside `--skills` and `--trigger-field`, and `--skills` still sets the competing set.
- **`round.json`.** `scope.selectedCases` is additive and absent on every other round. `allBundles` is false under `--case`. `scope.arms` is the arms the plan actually holds, so a trigger-only selection records `with-skill` alone and the title says so. `roundCatalogCases` extracts the regrade scope with the same `present` and `triggersOnly` semantics as before (an empty `present` still yields no cases) and adds the named-key filter. The regrade row pins that the rest of the bundle is not read as "added since".
- **Dry-run.** The `no-skill no skill` suffix now keys on whether every selected case is a trigger case. That is the same as the old `--triggers-only` test on every path that existed before, and right for a trigger-only `--case` selection. The card's acceptance line "`--dry-run --case` prints a plan holding only those cases" is met by the new `--case:` line plus the plan, and the PR body pastes both dry-runs.
- **Prose.** The `cli.ts` header now names `must_contain_any`. The README's unmet-group form, ``(none of: `a` / `b`)``, is what `summary.ts:217` builds with `code()`, and the `(lt)` / `(gt)` remark matches `summary.ts:186-191`. The `--case` README bullet and the changeset are true sentence by sentence against the code.
- **Self-test.** 40 to 44 rows, floor raised to match. The four rows cover the card's three acceptance rows plus regrade scope. The dev's ablation of `selectCases` reds the selection row, and the restore is recorded byte-identical.

**Nit, not owed.** The merged, still-unreleased `.changeset/37928-skill-evals-any-of.md` still renders the missed-column form as `(none of: a / b)` without per-token code spans, which is the same slip N4 fixed in the README. Fold it in here only if the head moves for another reason. Otherwise it can ride the next prose touch on this surface.

**Landing:** not governed, so the area lands it after ACCEPT.
